summary: AdEMAMix adds a slow gradient EMA to Adam-style state; account for the extra buffer and validate task quality.
restrictions: no AdEMAMix as a drop-in default for short, small-data, or memory-constrained runs
no comparison against untuned AdamW or mismatched token/step budgets

NVIDIA A10-specific benefit is not widely confirmed; treat AdEMAMix as a software optimizer experiment only for long-token or LLM-style training after a tuned AdamW baseline and an explicit optimizer-state memory budget.

summary: Compatible symmetric-memory collectives can overlap tensor-parallel communication with compute on multiple GPUs; this has no single-GPU benefit.
restrictions: multi-GPU only; recommended=true means candidate when tensor-parallel communication is a measured bottleneck and topology supports overlap, not a general single-card optimization; SymmetricMemory is alpha and Copy Engine collectives require NCCL 2.28+, P2P access, zero-CTA NCCL policy, symmetric-memory allocation, and rendezvous; official docs directly cover all_gather_into_tensor/all_to_all_single CE overlap, so reduce_scatter overlap is not assumed here; example_code + Nautilus run pending before verified=true

summary: A compatible fused classifier/cross-entropy implementation avoids materializing the full large-vocabulary logits tensor; validate the loss and gradient path before reuse.
restrictions: software technique for cross-entropy over a linear classifier/logit projection; strongest fit is large-vocabulary LM heads, but Apple documents the general logits = X @ A.T + b form; requires compatible PyTorch/Triton/CUDA stack for the Triton CCE path; little benefit when logits materialization is not a memory/time bottleneck; example_code + Nautilus run pending before verified=true

summary: Length bucketing and a short-to-long sequence curriculum change data order and attention boundaries; validate task compatibility before reuse.
restrictions: data-ordering technique for text sequence training; no hardware-specific acceleration and no direct inference benefit; example_code + Nautilus run pending before verified=true

summary: Muon applies a Newton-Schulz update to eligible matrix weights and uses a separate optimizer for other parameters; verify task quality and runtime before adoption.
restrictions: no Muon on embedding/bias/norm/head/non-2D params and no comparison against undertuned AdamW
no blind AdamW replacement in small CNN, tabular, inference, or memory-bound runs

software training optimizer; requires a PyTorch build that exposes torch.optim.Muon; no hardware-specific acceleration is required; use only on selected 2D hidden weights and keep AdamW for embeddings/bias/norm/head/non-2D params; benchmark against tuned AdamW; not an inference feature

summary: For an image-decode bottleneck, compatible nvImageCodec GPU decoding and DLPack transfer may overlap data loading with compute; check codec/hardware support. This does not apply to text workloads.
restrictions: GPU image-codec data pipeline; recommended=true only for CV/imaging pipelines where CPU image decode is a measured bottleneck, not for text/LLM-only workloads or storage/augmentation-bound pipelines; NVIDIA nvJPEG hardware-acceleration docs only list Ampere A100/A30 within Ampere, so dedicated hardware JPEG decode is not assumed for this card; uses hybrid/software/GPU codec paths where available; codec/plugin support is format-dependent; example_code + Nautilus run pending before verified=true

summary: SOAP applies Adam in the preconditioner eigenbasis with amortized eigendecomposition; verify memory, runtime and task quality before adoption.
restrictions: no SOAP as a universal default for small, latency-bound, or memory-constrained runs
no adoption without verifying the third-party SOAP package/API in the runtime

NVIDIA A10-specific benefit is not widely confirmed; treat SOAP as a software optimizer experiment only after a tuned AdamW baseline, with optimizer-step time, peak memory, and validation loss measured before adoption.
